subject: Number of individuals for population mean

messages.author: d993567db688249f
messages.subject: Number of individuals for population mean
parts:
Hi all,

I'd like to track the minimum number of animals in order to adequately estimate population home range and speed as part of our animal ethics considerations. 

I have some ideas (below) but would really appreciate an expert eye.
Do you think this is a good approach, or am I missing something?
The CV I've chosen is quite arbitrary, is there any better guidance out there?

We already have a sample from a similar population (14 individuals) and so my idea is to:
1. Plan sampling design using movedesign.
2. Estimate ctmm parameters and simulate tracks for additional individuals with the planned sampling design.
3. Use meta function to investigate population mean and CV for varying numbers of these individuals.
4. Choose the minimum number of individuals that gives a CV <= 0.10

Thank you

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Number of individuals for population mean
parts:
Hi Lisa,

The CoV returned by meta() is that of the population of home-range areas, and will stabilize with more data. Is your CV target the coefficient of variation of the estimate of the population mean w.r.t. its sampling distribution? If so, that makes sense. It might be easier to look at the CI width divided by the point estimate. Asymptotically, that width should shrink with 1/sqrt(N). So if you set your target on that, then you can work out what N needs to be with some algebra. I get:

N <- N0 * ( (CI[3]-CI[1])/CI[2]/MAX.WIDTH )^2

where N0 is the initial number (14) and MAX.WIDTH could be something like 20% or something.

Best,
Chris
